_comment: Hand-made mapping from Infer's native bug types to SEI CERT C rule ids
and CWE ids. It is DATA, not derived: every entry is a judgement about
what defect the bug type reports, made from Infer's issue-type
documentation (`infer help --list-issue-types`, v1.2.0), and the harness
records this file's sha256 into every run so a table can say which
version of the judgement it used. A bug type with no entry is reported
as `unmapped` -- counted, never dropped. `cert: []` means CERT C has no
rule for the defect; `cwe: []` likewise. Entries cover the C-relevant
types of the checkers Infer runs by default (pulse, liveness,
bufferoverrun, biabduction); the Java, Objective-C, C++-only and
Erlang types are left unmapped on purpose.
Where a bug type spans several Juliet CWEs, every one it can report is
listed, because the Juliet tables match a finding to a CWE directory
exactly. Add entries with a `note` saying why; change one only with a

NULLPTR_DEREFERENCE.note: pulse: dereference of a pointer that is null on some path

NULL_ARGUMENT.note: null passed where the callee dereferences it

PULSE_RESOURCE_LEAK.note: resource (in C, a FILE* or descriptor) not released; as cppcheck resourceLeak

USE_AFTER_FREE.note: access through a pointer after free; pulse reports a second free as this type too

USE_AFTER_LIFETIME.note: in C, access to an object after its storage duration ended

STACK_VARIABLE_ADDRESS_ESCAPE.note: address of a local escapes its scope

DEAD_STORE.note: liveness: value written and never read; as clang-analyzer DeadStores

BUFFER_OVERRUN_L1.note: bufferoverrun, most certain level; an offset past either end, read or write

BUFFER_OVERRUN_L4.note: as L1, less certain (not on by default)

BUFFER_OVERRUN_L5.note: as L1, least certain (not on by default)

INTEGER_OVERFLOW_L1.note: bufferoverrun's arithmetic overflow or underflow, signedness not distinguished

INTEGER_OVERFLOW_L5.note: as L1, least certain (not on by default)

INFERBO_ALLOC_IS_BIG.note: allocation size beyond a sane bound

CONSTANT_ADDRESS_DEREFERENCE.note: dereference of a fixed integer address; as clang-analyzer FixedAddressDereference has no CERT rule

CHECKERS_PRINTF_ARGS.note: printf arguments do not match the format

INHERENTLY_DANGEROUS_FUNCTION.note: call to a function that cannot be used safely
